item.title: Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware
item.description:
Exposed API Leads to Customer Credential Exposure at Radware

Cybersecurity company Radware experienced a data breach after an unauthorized party accessed an unauthenticated internal Cloud WAF management API left reachable from the public internet on November 19, 2026.

🔍 Incident Overview

Radware detected the unauthorized access on a Thursday, ten hours after the initial intrusion. Upon detection, the company took several immediate response actions:

  • Blocked the originating IP address and disabled public access to the internal management API.
  • Revoked and replaced all internal account credentials.
  • Initiated a root cause analysis report, which was later shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer.

Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.

⚙️ Impacted Systems and Data

The exposure was limited to specific account management details and log export configurations, while core traffic inspection remained unaffected.

System / Data Category Status According to Radware
Customer contact details Potentially accessed
Log export credentials (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, SFTP) Potentially accessed for a subset of customers
WAF traffic inspection and certificates Not exposed
End-users’ data and customer application traffic Not exposed
Cloud DDoS services and data Not exposed

Radware stated that WAF traffic inspection and protection have continued without interruption, with no evidence found of policy changes or access to customer application traffic.

💡 Customer Action Advised

Radware strongly advised affected AppSec (WAF, BOT) customers to take immediate remedial steps:

  • Rotate exposed Cloud WAF log export credentials, including Azure Blob Storage keys or SAS tokens, AWS S3 access keys, or SFTP credentials, as soon as possible.
  • Review access logs on cloud storage accounts for unexpected access dating back to at least November 19.

The company noted it has already received reports from customers regarding AWS alerts for an unfamiliar IP address attempting to access their log-export buckets.

📊 Investigation and Public Response

Radware is continuing to investigate the incident to determine whether any exposed API keys or customer information were used without authorization. As of the report, Radware has not issued a public statement, filed a breach report with the US Securities and Exchange Commission, or provided an immediate response to inquiries from BleepingComputer.

#Cybersecurity #DataBreach #Radware #CloudSecurity #APISecurity

Source: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys

item.title: AWS Enhances API and AI Endpoint Security
item.description:
AWS Enhances API and AI Endpoint Security

AWS has launched new capabilities to discover and protect APIs and AI endpoints, addressing the evolving landscape of digital business and AI agent interactions.

🔍 Overview

  • AWS has introduced new features to help discover and protect APIs and AI endpoints.
  • This includes API Portal in Amazon API Gateway, API Security, and AI Security managed rule groups in AWS WAF.

🧩 How it works

  • API Portal discovers APIs and AI endpoints from configuration and live traffic.
  • API Security protects against broken object level authorization, authentication attacks, and reconnaissance.
  • AI Security identifies AI traffic, validates requests, and checks prompts and responses through Amazon Bedrock Guardrails.

⚙️ Key details

  • API Portal is available in the Amazon API Gateway console.
  • API Security and AI Security are available in the AWS WAF console.
  • The new features work with Amazon CloudFront, Amazon API Gateway REST APIs, and Application Load Balancer.

🚀 Availability

  • API Portal, API Security, and AI Security are generally available today.

💡 Why it matters

  • APIs have run digital businesses for over a decade.
  • In 2026, AI endpoints joined them, leading to a need for new security measures.
  • AI agents now act on behalf of users, requiring robust protection of APIs and AI endpoints.

#AWS #APISecurity #AIEndpoints #CloudSecurity #DigitalBusiness

Source: Introducing API and AI security on AWS, from discovery to protection | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Qualys TotalAppSec Achieves FedRAMP High Authorization
item.description:
Qualys TotalAppSec Achieves FedRAMP High Authorization

🔎 Overview

Qualys TotalAppSec has been granted FedRAMP High authorization on the Qualys Government Platform (FedRAMP Certified Class D, package FR2231052341). The authorization positions the service within the federal high‑impact security boundary and enables agencies to use its continuous application‑security capabilities.

⚙️ What TotalAppSec Provides

  • Maintains 99.2%+ CISA KEV coverage with a 16‑hour median from CVE disclosure to detection.
  • Generates ATO and Continuous Monitoring (ConMon) evidence from within an authorized High boundary.
  • Detects and reports vulnerabilities at a cadence that meets the daily detection requirement for High‑impact assets.
  • Supports application‑layer asset tagging as required by CISA BOD 26‑04.

📜 Policy and Compliance Backdrop

  • NIST SP 800‑228 (updated March 2026) treats APIs as a distinct control surface, calling for inventories that include shadow and zombie APIs, runtime discovery, and reconciliation of declared specs against live traffic.
  • CISA BOD 26‑04 (issued June 10 2026) mandates risk‑based remediation and application‑layer asset tagging by December 7 2026. The directive replaces flat patch deadlines with urgency calculations that factor in exposure, KEV status, exploit automation, and technical impact.
  • For High‑impact findings, agencies must assess reachability and exploitability for each finding and conduct at‑least‑daily detection.
  • Non‑compliant offerings lose their authorization after March 7 2027, removing the right to sell to the government.

📈 Security Impact

  • Mean Time to Exploit (MTTE) is now estimated at minus seven days (M‑Trends 2026), indicating adversaries often act before a vulnerability is disclosed.
  • Agencies cannot out‑patch an adversary who starts before disclosure, underscoring the need for rapid detection.
  • Public‑facing applications are now the leading initial‑access vector (40 % of incidents) and 56 % of tracked vulnerabilities require no authentication to exploit.
  • Federal AI use cases have more than doubled to 3,611 across 56 agencies, with 445 designated high‑impact AI subject to OMB M‑25‑21 risk‑management practices. AI coding assistants have cleared FedRAMP authorization, and the GSA is asking agencies to build Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.

🚀 Availability and Next Steps

  • TotalAppSec’s FedRAMP High status enables immediate use by federal agencies seeking to meet the CISA BOD 26‑04 remediation timeline.
  • Agencies should integrate TotalAppSec into their application‑layer asset tagging processes and ensure continuous API discovery to satisfy NIST SP 800‑228 requirements.
  • Ongoing monitoring will be required to maintain daily detection and reporting compliance through the December 7 2026 deadline and beyond.

#FedRAMP #GovSec #APIsecurity #AICompliance

Source: Qualys TotalAppSec Is Now FedRAMP High Authorized | Qualys
